_doc: MATH-PROSE -> FUNCTION constructions (graph data, the agent's grammar). Each maps a math-prose CLAUSE (a phrase found WITHIN a real definition, e.g. an OEIS sequence_name) to the FORMAL function form in the index variable `n` that compute_grounding.comprehend_computational_definition grounds. The agent's construction grammar EXTRACTS the function from prose by clause-matching these + the embedded-formula path ('a(n) = <expr>'); the source's ground-truth values then VERIFY (and SELECT) the correct extraction. General patterns (count-of / sum-of / arithmetic), NOT per-sequence rules. Coverage grows by adding clauses — graph data, not code. The honest frontier = prose whose function no clause/formula extracts (recursive, idiomatic, multi-clause).

clauses.name: sum_of_the_divisors
clauses.clause: sum of the divisors of n

_doc_recursive: ORDER-N (recursive) constructions. The FLAT clauses above match a WHOLE string -> NONE on anything compositional. These constructions COMPOSE: a construction's SLOT content is itself comprehended by (sub-)constructions, recursively, bottoming out at a comprehension-BEDROCK (an atomic term / held set-member primitive). This is the agent's order-N operator (order_n_composition.iterate_to_n) applied to the construction grammar: the COMBINATION rule = 'fill a slot by comprehending its content', the BEDROCK = a member-form leaf. Each leaf/recursive construction comprehends to a MEMBER-FORM: a partial structure {value, predicate} over the binder k in 1..n (value = what to accumulate for member k; predicate = a multiplicative 0/1 mask selecting which k are members). An AGGREGATOR (sum/number) wraps a member-form into a runnable sum{k in 1..n : value*predicate} formula. Composition: 'the sum of [the squares of [the divisors of n]] that are [less than n]' = aggregator(sum) over a value-map(square) over a member-set(divisors) under a filter(less than n).

member_forms.name: divisors_of_n
member_forms._doc: BEDROCK member-form: k is a member iff k divides n; the member's own value is k.

member_forms.name: integers
member_forms._doc: BEDROCK: every k in the range is a member; value k.

value_maps.name: squares_of
value_maps._doc: RECURSIVE: 'squares of [X]' comprehends X (a member-form) then maps each member's value v -> v*v; the membership predicate is inherited from X.

_doc_no_cubes: NOTE: 'cubes of' is deliberately NOT seeded here. It is ACQUIRED BY READING its meta-definition ('the cubes of a set means each member multiplied by itself three times') via construction_grammar.acquire_construction — the 'read about how to read' proof: BEFORE the read, 'sum of cubes of divisors of n' (A001158) comprehends to NONE; AFTER, it parses + reproduces the OEIS values.

filters.name: less_than_n
filters._doc: RECURSIVE filter: narrows the membership predicate of the inner member-form by ANDing a 0/1 mask (k<n).

filters.name: odd
filters._doc: PRE-modifier filter ('odd divisors of n'): mask k%2 (==1 for odd).

aggregators.name: sum_of
aggregators._doc: AGGREGATOR: 'sum of [SET]' wraps the comprehended member-form SET into a runnable sum over k in 1..n, accumulating value*predicate (predicate masks non-members to 0).

aggregators.name: number_of
aggregators._doc: AGGREGATOR: 'number of [SET]' COUNTS members (sum of the membership predicate over k).

_doc_operator_tree: GENERIC OPERATOR-TREE constructions for the RESEARCH FRONTIER. Where the member-form grammar above produces a runnable number-theory formula, these produce a STRUCTURE TREE — op(args) nested — for compositional research prose whose OPERATIONS are not yet held as runnable primitives. comprehend_structure composes them RECURSIVELY (a slot is filled by comprehending its content), bottoming out at an ATOMIC TERM (a held concept / named object). This is how 'the kernel of the boundary operator modulo its image' comprehends: [A] modulo [B] over kernel of [X] over the boundary operator + image of [X] -> modulo(kernel(boundary_operator), image(boundary_operator)). The agent COMPOSES the homology STRUCTURE; the kernel/image OPERATIONS being un-held is the NAMED residual (acquirable the same way by reading). Each construction names whether its head OP is held_runnable (the agent can compute it) — kernel/image/modulo over operators are NOT, the precise stall.
_doc_new_families: THE READER-FRONTIER FAMILIES (homology / betti / dimension / fundamental_group / genus) live in the SAME `operators` table below. Each is the SAME prefix operator-of-object construction euler_characteristic already is — a DATA ROW, read by the uniform prefix loop in _comprehend_structure, NOT a per-operator Python branch. An operator whose `indexed` is true carries an `{index}` slot in its pattern that the SAME uniform _match_indexed_operator/_read_index mechanism reads (an ordinal 'second', a symbolic 'n th'/'k th', or a bare number) into the typed tree's `index` slot via the seeded `index_words`/`index_symbols` tables. Adding a sixth/seventh operator = another row here, no code change (the generality proof). The OPERATION (computing homology/betti/...) is un-held here (`held_runnable`: false) — typing is the reader rung; it then STALLS DOWNSTREAM at generate/compute (no _presupposed_needs branch, no compute faculty) until those rungs follow.

operators.name: modulo
operators._doc: QUOTIENT '[A] modulo [B]' (here A/B as a quotient group, not integer mod) -> modulo(A, B). The infix splits on 'modulo'; both slots comprehended recursively. 'its image' resolves the possessive to the same operand the sibling kernel reads.

operators.name: kernel_of
operators._doc: 'kernel of [X]' -> kernel(X): the set of inputs the map X sends to zero. The OPERATION is un-held (acquirable by reading its meta-def).

operators.name: image_of
operators._doc: 'image of [X]' -> image(X): the set of outputs of the map X. Un-held.

operators.name: rank_of
operators._doc: 'rank of [X]' -> rank(X): the invariant 'rank' of the object X (for a free group, the number of free generators; for an abelian group, the free rank). The OPERATION is un-held as a runnable compute here — but the asked-invariant TYPE is what the comprehension needs (the rank invariant OF a sub-object).

operators.name: number_of_free_generators_of
operators._doc: 'the number of free generators of [X]' -> free_rank(X): the free-group rank invariant under a different SURFACE (the paraphrase the generality demo rides on). The general reader types it to the SAME free-rank-of-kernel invariant; a regex keyed to 'free group' would MISS this phrasing.

operators.name: euler_characteristic_of
operators._doc: SECOND INVARIANT (cmsg120, the breadth-of-two): 'the euler characteristic of [X]' -> euler_characteristic(X). A prefix operator the SAME order-N reader composes (its slot comprehended recursively, bottoming at the object atom). The well-definedness PRESUPPOSITION (chi well-defined => a FINITE complex => total Betti finite) is DERIVED from this typed term + READ facts (the alternating-sum + finiteness theorems), NOT a per-invariant regex. The OPERATION (computing chi) is un-held here; the asked-invariant TYPE is what the comprehension needs (the chi invariant OF an object).

operators.name: homology_indexed_of
operators._doc: INDEXED 'the n-th homology of [X]' -> homology(X, index=n): the n-th homology GROUP/module. The {index} slot reads the dimension index (ordinal 'second' -> 2, symbolic 'n th'/'k th' -> n/k, subscript 'h 1' surface handled by the index reader). The SAME prefix mechanism, one index slot wider.

operators.name: homology_of
operators._doc: UN-INDEXED 'the homology of [X]' -> homology(X): the (graded/total) homology, no dimension index given. Plain prefix operator-of-object.

operators.name: betti_indexed_number_of
operators._doc: INDEXED 'the second betti number of [X]' -> betti(X, index=2): the rank of the n-th homology. The {index} reads the same ordinal/symbolic forms as homology ('second'->2, 'n th'->n, 'b 2' subscript). Indexed handled GENERALLY (the index reader is shared), not a betti special-case.

operators.name: betti_number_of
operators._doc: UN-INDEXED 'the betti number of [X]' -> betti(X): the Betti number with no dimension specified.

operators.name: homology_subscript_of
operators._doc: SUBSCRIPT surface 'H_1 of [X]' -> homology(X, index=1). The LaTeX/subscript surface 'H_1' tokenises (lowercased [a-z0-9]+) to ['h','1']; the operator-name token 'h' is the pattern literal, the bare number '1' is read by the SAME uniform _read_index into the index slot. Subscript handled GENERALLY (one DATA row + the shared index reader), not a per-operator regex.

operators.name: betti_subscript_of
operators._doc: SUBSCRIPT surface 'b_2 of [X]' -> betti(X, index=2). 'b_2' tokenises to ['b','2']; the same index reader fills the slot.

operators.name: dimension_of
operators._doc: 'the dimension of [X]' -> dimension(X): the (topological/Krull/vector-space) dimension invariant. Plain prefix operator-of-object — a DATA ROW, not a branch.

operators.name: fundamental_group_of
operators._doc: 'the fundamental group of [X]' -> fundamental_group(X): pi_1 of the space X. A multi-token prefix ('fundamental group of') read by the same prefix loop. NOTE: the BARE atom 'the fundamental group' (no 'of X') still types as the seeded fundamental_group ATOM for the rank-of-pi_1 control; this operator only fires when an object follows ('... of X').

operators.name: genus_of
operators._doc: 'the genus of [X]' -> genus(X): the genus invariant of a surface/curve. Plain prefix operator-of-object — a DATA ROW.

_doc_index_words: INDEX VOCABULARY for INDEXED operators (betti_i, homology_i). The uniform index-reader in _comprehend_structure reads an operator's {index} slot against these DATA rows: an ORDINAL surface ('zeroth'..'tenth', 'first'..) maps to its integer; a SYMBOLIC surface ('n'/'k'/'i'/'j'/'m' optionally with a trailing 'th'/'st'/'nd'/'rd' the tokeniser split off, e.g. 'n-th' -> ['n','th']) maps to the symbol; a BARE NUMBER token maps to itself. Subscript surfaces ('H_1','b_2') tokenise to ['h','1']/['b','2'] — the operator-name token is consumed by the operator pattern, the bare number by this table. Teaching a new ordinal = a row, not code; the index handling is GENERAL across every indexed operator, not per-operator.
_doc_qualifiers: POSTFIX TYPING QUALIFIERS for the RESEARCH FRONTIER. A trailing qualifier RE-TYPES the invariant it modifies: 'the rank of X AS A FREE GROUP' is not the generic `rank` but the FREE-GROUP rank `free_rank` (the number of free generators). The discrimination is the GRAMMAR'S, by the qualifier — an UNQUALIFIED 'the rank of X' stays the generic `rank` op (so a control 'the rank of the fundamental group' types to `rank`, NOT free_rank, and the finite-free-rank presupposition does NOT fire). comprehend_structure tries a qualifier construction LAST (after the bare structure comprehends): the qualifier pattern is a TRAILING literal sequence; the head it modifies is the inner structure comprehended recursively; `retype` says which op the (single-arg) head is re-typed to (rank -> free_rank). This is the SAME order-N composition the prefix/infix operators use, one register wider (a postfix modifier). A regex keyed to 'free group' would put free_rank there by string-match; here the reader reads the qualifier as part of the STRUCTURE.

qualifiers.name: as_a_free_group
qualifiers._doc: '[the rank of X] as a free group' -> free_rank(X): a rank TAKEN in the category of free groups = the number of free generators. Re-types a `rank` head to `free_rank`; leaves any other head unchanged (the qualifier only re-types a rank).

qualifiers.name: as_a_free_abelian_group
qualifiers._doc: '[the rank of X] as a free abelian group' -> free_rank(X): the free-abelian rank = the number of free generators of the free part. Same free-rank typing.

_doc_definition_binding: DEFINITION-BINDING constructions (the cmsg-gap-1 fix). A question STEM INTRODUCES its objects ('Let X be a <type>', 'Let X denote the <type>', 'We denote by X the <type>'). The reader reads these binding clauses into a LOCAL TYPED ENVIRONMENT (symbol -> a typed object) so the invariant's `{object}` slot RESOLVES against the stem's introductions, NOT a fixed global atom list. This is GENERAL (any introduced object binds + types) and graph-resident: a binding clause is a surface PATTERN ({sym} <copula/denote> a/the {type}); the {type} is normalised to a structural object-TYPE via `binding_types` below. A bound symbol then behaves as an atom whose `term` is the type. The patterns are DATA — teaching a new binding surface = adding a clause, not code. The euler/genus/rank operators compose over the bound object exactly as over a seeded atom.

binding_clauses.name: we_denote_by_the
binding_clauses._doc: 'We denote by X the <type>' -> bind X to an object of <type> (e.g. 'We denote by K_k the complete graph on k vertices').

binding_clauses.name: let_denote_the
binding_clauses._doc: 'Let X denote the <type>' -> bind X (e.g. 'Let Delta_k denote the abstract simplicial complex defined as follows').

binding_clauses.name: let_be_a
binding_clauses._doc: 'Let X be a <type>' (also 'Let G be a group ...') -> bind X. The generality demo rides on this: ANY introduced object binds + types, not a Delta_k special-case.

_doc_binding_types: TYPE NORMALISATION for definition-binding. A bound clause's <type> surface (a noun phrase, possibly with a trailing 'on k vertices' / 'defined as follows' qualifier) is normalised to a STRUCTURAL object-type by matching a HEAD type-noun here (longest first). This is a canonical math-object-type vocabulary (graph DATA), NOT a per-question atom: it lists the TYPES (simplicial complex, graph, group, ...), so a stem introducing ANY object of these types binds + types. The reduced-Euler / rank / genus operators only need the slot to RESOLVE to a typed object; the specific type drives which compute faculty the object's definition is handed to (a simplicial_complex with a read face-predicate -> the chi compute).
_doc_object_atoms: GENERIC OBJECT-ATOM bedrock for the OBJECT SLOT (the bucket-B comprehension frontier). An invariant operator ('rank of', 'dimension of', 'genus of', 'Euler characteristic of', 'homology of') types fine, but its `{x}` object slot bottomed out at a tiny hand-atom list ('x'/'the space'/'the complex'), so 'rank of E' / 'Euler characteristic of the quotient stack [U/G]' / 'rank of the Neron-Severi group of X' returned None -> bucket B. This block widens what the object slot TYPES TO, GENERALLY (data, not a regex-per-question): a token run is a generic OBJECT when it (a) carries a recognised OBJECT-TYPE-NOUN head ('group'/'space'/'stack'/'manifold'/'curve'/'variety'/'sheaf'/'scheme'/'module'/'ring'/'subgroup'/'subspace'/'hypergraph'/...) -> typed as that object-type, OR (b) is a pure NOTATION/SYMBOL run (single-letter atoms, digits, Greek names, connectives like 'times'/'oplus', applied-notation like pi_3(X)/H^2(G,M)/[U/G]/E(Q)) -> typed as a notation object. The recogniser (comprehend_object_atom) is PRECISE: arbitrary prose with no type-noun and non-symbol words does NOT type (stays a miss, zero false-positive). The object types -> the clause types -> it flows to the held stack (formalize/construct/compute); where the stack has no compute for that object it is an HONEST type-but-stall, now correctly TYPED. object_type_nouns / notation_symbols / object_connectives are the vocabulary (graph DATA); a new object-type = a row, not code.

atoms.name: boundary_operator
atoms._doc: ATOM (comprehension-bedrock): the boundary operator ∂ — a HELD operation (acquired in acquire_boundary_operator). The recursion bottoms out here.

atoms.name: hurewicz_map
atoms._doc: ATOM: the Hurewicz homomorphism h_*: pi_1 -> H_1 (the abelianization map in dimension 1). A NAMED math object the agent reads; the recursion bottoms out here. NOT held-runnable as a computed object — its facts (kernel = commutator subgroup, index = |H_1|) are acquired by READING as Claims, not hard-coded.

atoms.name: abelianization_map
atoms._doc: ATOM: the abelianization map pi_1 -> pi_1/[pi_1,pi_1] = H_1 — the SAME object as the Hurewicz map in dimension 1 (a paraphrase the general reader types identically). The generality demo rides on this: a paraphrase typed to the same term.

atoms.name: fundamental_group
atoms._doc: ATOM: the fundamental group pi_1. Lets the CONTROL 'the rank of the fundamental group' type to rank(fundamental_group) — the GENERIC rank, NOT free_rank (no 'as a free group' qualifier), so the finite-free-rank presupposition does NOT fire. The discrimination is the grammar's, by the absent qualifier.

atoms.name: space_x
atoms._doc: ATOM (comprehension-bedrock): the object/space X the invariant is asked OF. A NAMED placeholder object the reader bottoms out at, so 'the euler characteristic of X' / 'the genus of X' comprehend to euler_characteristic(space) / genus(space). The object's forward-model properties (b0/b1/b2/torsion) are what the derived presupposition collapses against in the gate; the atom itself is not held-runnable (no specific space).

atoms.name: space_simplicial_complex
atoms._doc: ATOM: a simplicial complex, read as the universal object/space the invariant is asked OF — the SAME `space` term the reader bottoms out at for 'the complex' / 'the cw complex'. Added as graph DATA (not Python) by the agent's own decision (jabberwock_decides_order1_lever): the binary-admissibility selector ranked the READER's Level-2 atom coverage the top lever because the lone token 'simplicial' was blocking euler/reduced-euler/betti invariant families from typing at all (typed=None) — upstream of the order-1 generator, which never even ran. Widening this atom lets those families TYPE, so the whole READ->GENERATE->ROUTE->DERIVE pipeline can run on them.
